pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
src/index.js defaults the view to open. test/done.test.js 'AC-2' checks both / and ?view=open return the open items in id order.
test 'AC-3' marks items 3 and 1 done and checks '✓ First item' then '✓ Third item'.
test 'AC-4' checks all three items in id order with only the done one marked.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav markup for each view and for /.
test 'AC-6' checks Open, closed, empty and __proto__ each give 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.

The code implements it, but no test names AC-7. The follow-up commit b521dd1 removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the only test that covers it. The spec has no 'verified by review' mark for this item, so under the naming rule it is unmet.
traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all. test 'AC-8' checks it.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits' (b521dd1), renamed the AC-7 test and dropped the 'AC-7' id from its title. No test now names AC-7, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'. The commit message hides this by calling it a follow-up edit.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7:' in the test title, so the test is named by the acceptance item it proves.

findings.what: The PR's engineering details say test/done.test.js 'covers AC-1 to AC-8'. That is untrue by the test names, because AC-7 is not named.
findings.fix: Fix once the AC-7 name is restored.

lenses.note: The spec has a go, and the decisions are followed: open is the default and the view is a query parameter.
AC-7 is unnamed in the tests after the last commit. All six state-table rows have tests.
The assertions check behaviour and would fail on wrong code. I did not run npm test; CI runs it. The traffic fake and the traffic-config check changes are covered by tests.
The README describes the views. The spec is accurate.
Query parameters are handled correctly. Object.hasOwn blocks __proto__. The empty-table fallback works. The migration is additive.
Titles are HTML-escaped. The view value is checked against an allowlist. The SQL fragments are constants and never come from user input. No planted instructions found.
The page is minimal HTML with a nav. There is no styling and no UI files such as CSS or components.
No browser flow is involved. Behaviour is covered by HTTP-level tests.
The title is short and accurate. The claim that done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8 is false because of the AC-7 rename.
